newsitem.title: USA: HFS, CUC slump as merger review extended.
newsitem.headline: HFS, CUC slump as merger review extended.

text.p: Shares in merger partners HFS Inc and CUC International Inc slumped Monday after the companies said U.S. antitrust regulators made a second request for details on their proposed $11 billion merger, announced May 27.
Arbitrageurs and traders said the latest request, which centered on the companies' vacation timeshare exchange operations, does not mean the deal will not go through.
Late in the trading day, CUC shares fell 5/16, or 1.3 percent, to 23-13/16 in unusually active trade, while HFS shares were off one, or 1.8 percent, to 55-3/4.
The companies said the U.S. Federal Trade Commission asked the companies Friday for the additional information.

"They companies gave a lot of comfort in the news release (announcing the FTC second request). And in the conference call when the deal was first announced they said they would divest, do what they needed to do, to get the deal done," said an arb who declined to be identified.

The companies said in the news release early Monday afternoon that they did not expect any financial impact if a divestiture were required to complete the merger, nor did they expect a delay to the deal's closing.
CUC and HFS said they will meet in the next several weeks to discuss the possible divestiture of Interval International, CUC's timeshare exchange business.
Terms of their merger agreement call for 2.4031 CUC shares to be exchanged for each HFS share.
When the deal was announced, CUC said it expected to issue about 434 million shares, worth about $11 billion, to affect the swap.
